Tornadoes are spinning columns of air. They can pick up trees, cars, and even houses. Tornadoes usually appear as a dark funnel shape coming down from a storm cloud.

Image: A photo shows a dark gray funnel-shaped cloud touching the ground. Dust and debris swirl around the base.

What does the photo show?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A tornado with its funnel shape and spinning debris

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rainbow in the sky after a storm

choices.label: C
choices.text: A cloud that looks like a mushroom

choices.label: D
choices.text: A snowstorm covering a neighborhood

items.explanation: The photo shows a dark funnel cloud touching the ground with debris swirling around it, which matches the article's description of a tornado.

Humpback whales are the largest animals on Earth. They breathe air through a blowhole on top of their heads. When they breathe out, a spout of mist shoots up into the air.

Image: A photo shows the back of a large dark whale in the ocean. A tall white spout of mist shoots up from the whale's back.

What key idea does the photo help you understand?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That whales can live on land

choices.label: B
choices.text: What the blowhole spout looks like when a whale breathes out

choices.label: C
choices.text: How whales swim underwater

choices.label: D
choices.text: What a whale's tail looks like

items.explanation: The photo shows the mist spout coming from the whale's blowhole, which is the key detail the text describes about how whales breathe.

Honey is made by bees. Worker bees collect nectar from flowers and bring it back to the hive. In the hive, bees turn the nectar into honey by fanning it with their wings to remove water.

Image: A diagram shows four steps with arrows: (1) a bee on a flower collecting nectar, (2) the bee flying to a hive, (3) bees inside the hive fanning the nectar, (4) a jar of honey.

What does the diagram show about honey-making?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That bees only work at night

choices.label: B
choices.text: The four steps bees take to make honey

choices.label: C
choices.text: What different types of flowers look like

choices.label: D
choices.text: How a hive is built out of wood

items.explanation: The diagram shows all four steps of honey-making from nectar collection to the finished jar, illustrating the process described in the text.

The layers of the atmosphere surround Earth like a blanket of air. The troposphere is the lowest layer, where weather happens. Above it is the stratosphere, which contains the ozone layer that protects Earth from the sun's harmful rays. Higher layers include the mesosphere and thermosphere.

Image: A diagram shows a curved slice of the atmosphere above Earth. Starting from the ground and going upward: a blue band labeled 'Troposphere (weather),' a yellow band labeled 'Stratosphere (ozone layer),' a light purple band labeled 'Mesosphere,' and a very faint band labeled 'Thermosphere.'

What does the diagram contribute to the text's explanation of the atmosphere?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It shows that all layers of the atmosphere are the same thickness

choices.label: B
choices.text: It shows the order and relative thickness of each atmospheric layer above Earth

choices.label: C
choices.text: It explains why weather only happens in the troposphere

choices.label: D
choices.text: It shows how far away the moon is from Earth

items.explanation: The diagram shows the layers stacked in order from the ground up and uses different thicknesses for each band, giving readers a visual sense of how the layers are arranged and sized.

Soil is made of layers. The top layer is called topsoil and is rich in nutrients that help plants grow. Below that is subsoil, which has fewer nutrients. The bottom layer is bedrock, which is solid rock.

Image: A diagram shows a cross-section of the ground with three horizontal bands. The top dark brown band is labeled 'Topsoil.' The middle tan band is labeled 'Subsoil.' The bottom gray band with cracks is labeled 'Bedrock.' Plant roots reach down into the topsoil.

A student says the diagram helps explain why farmers care so much about topsoil. Why is this student correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The diagram shows that topsoil is at the very bottom, closest to the bedrock

choices.label: B
choices.text: The diagram shows that plant roots grow into the topsoil, and the text says topsoil has nutrients plants need

choices.label: C
choices.text: The diagram shows that bedrock is dark brown like topsoil

choices.label: D
choices.text: The diagram shows that subsoil is thicker than topsoil

items.explanation: The plant roots in the diagram visually connect to the topsoil layer, and the text explains that topsoil has nutrients. Together, they show why topsoil is critical for growing plants.

A Venn diagram is a tool used to compare two things. Two overlapping circles are drawn. Each circle represents one thing. The space where the circles overlap shows what the two things have in common.

Image: A Venn diagram shows two overlapping circles. The left circle is labeled 'Dolphins' and contains 'lives in ocean, has fins.' The right circle is labeled 'Dogs' and contains 'lives on land, has fur.' The overlapping section in the middle contains 'mammal, breathes air.'

How does the Venn diagram help clarify the main idea of the text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It shows that dolphins and dogs are exactly the same animal

choices.label: B
choices.text: It shows a real example of how overlapping circles are used to compare two things and show shared traits

choices.label: C
choices.text: It explains that dolphins are not mammals because they live in water

choices.label: D
choices.text: It shows that dogs have fins and dolphins have fur

items.explanation: The Venn diagram is a real example that demonstrates exactly what the text describes: circles for each subject, with the overlap showing shared traits. Seeing it in use clarifies how the tool works.

When light passes through a prism, it bends. Different colors of light bend different amounts. Violet light bends the most. Red light bends the least. This is why light separates into a rainbow of colors when it passes through a prism.

Image: A diagram shows a white beam of light entering the left side of a triangular prism. On the right side, the beam spreads into seven colored bands fanning out in order: red at the top (least bent), then orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet at the bottom (most bent). The colors are labeled.

Which statement best explains how the image and text work together?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The image shows the same information as the text, so only one is needed

choices.label: B
choices.text: The text explains why colors separate and the image shows what the separation looks like and proves which color bends most

choices.label: C
choices.text: The image is more accurate than the text because it shows the actual colors

choices.label: D
choices.text: The text explains what a prism is and the image shows a different type of prism

items.explanation: The text explains the scientific reason colors separate (they bend different amounts). The image shows the visual result and places violet at the bottom (most bent) and red at the top (least bent), which confirms the text's claim visually.

Glaciers are giant, slow-moving rivers of ice. As a glacier moves downhill over thousands of years, it carves valleys into the rock below. Glaciers that carved V-shaped river valleys into U-shaped valleys left behind a landscape that looks very different from one shaped by water alone.

Image: Two side-by-side diagrams are shown. The left diagram is labeled 'River Valley' and shows a V-shaped cross-section cut into rock. The right diagram is labeled 'Glacier Valley' and shows a wide U-shaped cross-section with steep sides and a flat bottom.

A classmate says the before-and-after diagrams are the most important part of this article. Which explanation best supports that claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The diagrams are most important because they show two different colors of rock

choices.label: B
choices.text: The diagrams are most important because the text uses the terms V-shaped and U-shaped but without seeing them drawn, it is nearly impossible to understand what the difference looks like

choices.label: C
choices.text: The diagrams are most important because they show how fast glaciers move compared to rivers

choices.label: D
choices.text: The diagrams are most important because the text does not explain what a glacier is

items.explanation: The text uses geometric terms (V-shaped and U-shaped) that are difficult to visualize without a picture. The side-by-side diagrams make the difference between the two valley shapes immediately clear, which is the central claim of the article.
